headline: Drivers face three-hour wait for Tk100 gas amid shortages
summary: CNG drivers are spending hours in long queues to refuel, while protests have erupted in Jamalpur over the crisis.
details: CNG drivers are facing severe hardships as they wait up to three hours in long queues just to get 100 Taka worth of gas.
The shortage has become so acute that some drivers are falling asleep in their vehicles while waiting for their turn at refueling stations.
In Jamalpur, the situation escalated into protests, where drivers blocked the highway to demand a steady supply of gas.
These fuel shortages are coinciding with ongoing load-shedding, adding to the daily struggles of transport workers and commuters.
The crisis is impacting the livelihoods of thousands of drivers who rely on CNGs for their daily income.

headline_marked: Power crisis deepens as [[load shedding reaches Dhaka]]
headline: Power crisis deepens as load shedding reaches Dhaka
summary: The capital city faces electricity outages as the energy crisis worsens, while officials promise relief soon via FSRU repairs.
details: Dhaka is now experiencing load shedding as the national power crisis continues to deepen, affecting residents and businesses across the capital.
The situation has sparked criticism, with Parwar blaming the government for the ongoing power and gas shortages.
In response, the Energy Minister has stated that the energy crisis is expected to ease soon.
The Minister noted that the relief will come once repairs to the Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) are completed.
The FSRU is critical for the country's liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply, which fuels many of the power plants.
caption:
Dhaka is facing power outages as the energy crisis worsens. When will the relief come?

Dhaka is now experiencing load shedding as the national power crisis continues to deepen, affecting residents and businesses across the capital.

The situation has sparked criticism, with Parwar blaming the government for the ongoing power and gas shortages.

In response, the Energy Minister has stated that the energy crisis is expected to ease soon.

The Minister noted that the relief will come once repairs to the Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) are completed.

The FSRU is critical for the country's liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply, which fuels many of the power plants.

Source: Dhaka Tribune
